recipes.title: Smoked salmon kedgeree, light
recipes.summary: A lighter British kedgeree with smoky salmon, softly spiced rice and boiled eggs. Spring onions and lemon juice keep the breakfast fresh and savoury.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice in water with half the salt until tender, then drain it well.
Boil the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks are firm but not dry.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Stir the cumin, paprika and turmeric into the onion until fragrant.
Fold the salmon, whole milk and cooked white rice through the spiced onion until hot.
Peel and quarter the eggs, then fold them through with the spring onions, lemon juice and remaining salt.
Rest the kedgeree off the heat so the rice absorbs the smoky, spiced flavours.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served freshly cooked. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat gently with a splash of whole milk. Do not leave the rice at room temperature, and do not freeze the boiled eggs.

recipes.title: Smoked salmon kedgeree
recipes.summary: A comforting British breakfast of smoky salmon, golden spiced rice and boiled eggs. Butter, spring onions and lemon bring the traditional kedgeree flavours together.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice in water with half the salt until tender, then drain it well.
Boil the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Stir the cumin, paprika and turmeric into the onion until fragrant.
Fold the salmon, whole milk and cooked white rice through the spiced onion until steaming hot.
Peel and quarter the eggs, then fold them through with the spring onions, lemon juice and remaining salt.
Rest the kedgeree off the heat so the rice absorbs the buttery, smoky flavours.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate promptly for up to 2 days and reheat gently until steaming throughout. Add a splash of whole milk if the rice feels dry. The finished dish is not ideal for freezing.

recipes.title: Smoked salmon kedgeree, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous British kedgeree with extra smoked salmon, rice and eggs. The buttery curry spices make it a substantial breakfast without losing the dish's bright lemon finish.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice in water with half the salt until tender, then drain it thoroughly.
Boil the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks are firm but still tender.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and cook the onion until completely soft and translucent.
Stir the cumin, paprika and turmeric into the onion until fragrant.
Fold the salmon, whole milk and cooked white rice through the spiced onion until evenly heated.
Peel and quarter the eggs, then fold them through with the spring onions, lemon juice and remaining salt.
Rest the kedgeree off the heat so the larger portion absorbs the buttery spices.

recipes.storageNotes: Best fresh, though leftovers keep for up to 2 days in the refrigerator. Reheat until steaming with a little whole milk. The eggs and rice lose quality if frozen.

recipes.title: Jamaican rice and peas, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Jamaican lunch of coconut rice and kidney beans scented with thyme, spring onions and allspice. More beans and less rice make it satisfying while preserving the traditional character.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the spring onions and garlic so their flavour can infuse the cooking liquid.
Combine the coconut milk, vegetable broth, kidney beans, spring onions, garlic, thyme, allspice and salt in a large saucepan.
Bring the coconut mixture to a steady boil over medium-high heat.
Stir in the white rice, cover the pan and simmer gently until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest the covered rice and peas off the heat so the grains finish steaming.
Remove the spring onions and fluff the white rice and kidney beans gently before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat until steaming with a splash of vegetable broth. Cool the rice promptly after cooking. Freeze in portions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Jamaican rice and peas
recipes.summary: Classic Jamaican rice and peas cooked in coconut milk with kidney beans, thyme and allspice. It is fragrant, comforting and substantial enough for a simple lunch.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the spring onions and garlic so they release their flavour evenly.
Combine the coconut milk, vegetable broth, kidney beans, spring onions, garlic, thyme, allspice and salt in a large saucepan.
Bring the coconut mixture to a steady boil over medium-high heat.
Stir in the white rice, cover the pan and simmer gently until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest the covered rice and peas off the heat so the rice finishes steaming.
Remove the spring onions and fluff the white rice and kidney beans gently before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheat thoroughly with a small splash of vegetable broth. Cool leftovers quickly. Freeze individual portions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Jamaican rice and peas, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Jamaican rice and peas with extra rice, beans and creamy coconut milk. Thyme and allspice give the large shared pot its unmistakable Caribbean aroma.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the spring onions and garlic so they can flavour the larger pot evenly.
Combine the coconut milk, vegetable broth, kidney beans, spring onions, garlic, thyme, allspice and salt in a large saucepan.
Bring the coconut mixture to a steady boil over medium-high heat.
Stir in the white rice, cover the pan and simmer gently until tender and all the liquid is absorbed.
Rest the covered rice and peas off the heat so the larger batch finishes steaming evenly.
Remove the spring onions and fluff the white rice and kidney beans gently before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate promptly for up to 3 days and reheat with a little vegetable broth. The rice and peas freeze well in portions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Kartoffelpuffer with mushroom sauce, light
recipes.summary: Crisp German potato pancakes served with a creamy mushroom and thyme sauce. The lighter version uses less oil and sour cream while keeping the pancakes golden and satisfying.

steps.instruction: Grate the potato and onion using the coarse side of a box grater.
Squeeze the grated potato and onion firmly in a clean towel to remove excess liquid.
Combine the potato, onion, eggs, wheat flour, paprika and half the salt into a thick batter.
Shape the potato mixture into twelve thin, even pancakes.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the potato pancakes in batches until crisp and golden on both sides, adding the remaining vegetable oil as needed.
Cook the mushrooms in the empty pan until browned and their released moisture has evaporated.
Stir the sour cream, whole milk, thyme and remaining salt into the mushrooms.
Simmer the mushroom sauce gently until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Serve the crisp Kartoffelpuffer with the warm mushroom sauce spooned alongside.

recipes.storageNotes: The pancakes are best freshly fried. Refrigerate pancakes and sauce separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the pancakes in the oven or a dry pan. Freeze the pancakes for up to 2 months, but not the sauce.

recipes.title: Kartoffelpuffer with mushroom sauce
recipes.summary: Traditional-style German potato pancakes with crisp edges and a savoury mushroom cream sauce. They make a comforting vegetarian dinner for sharing.

steps.instruction: Grate the potato and onion using the coarse side of a box grater.
Squeeze the grated potato and onion firmly in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as possible.
Combine the potato, onion, eggs, wheat flour, paprika and half the salt into a thick batter.
Shape the potato mixture into twelve even pancakes.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the potato pancakes in batches until deeply golden and crisp, adding the remaining vegetable oil as needed.
Cook the mushrooms in the empty pan until browned and their moisture has evaporated.
Stir the sour cream, whole milk, thyme and remaining salt into the mushrooms.
Simmer the mushroom sauce gently until creamy and thick enough to coat the pancakes.
Serve the Kartoffelpuffer immediately with the mushroom sauce spooned alongside.

recipes.storageNotes: Store the pancakes and mushroom sauce separately for up to 3 days. Reheat pancakes in a hot oven or dry frying pan to restore their crispness. Freeze only the pancakes for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Kartoffelpuffer with mushroom sauce, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous platter of crisp German potato pancakes with a rich mushroom, sour cream and thyme sauce. The larger batch makes a substantial vegetarian dinner for four.

steps.instruction: Grate the potato and onion using the coarse side of a box grater.
Squeeze the grated potato and onion firmly in a clean towel until little liquid remains.
Combine the potato, onion, eggs, wheat flour, paprika and half the salt into a thick batter.
Shape the potato mixture into sixteen even pancakes.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the potato pancakes in batches until deeply golden and crisp, adding the remaining vegetable oil as needed.
Cook the mushrooms in the empty pan until browned and their released moisture has evaporated.
Stir the sour cream, whole milk, thyme and remaining salt into the mushrooms.
Simmer the mushroom sauce gently until rich and thick enough to cling to a spoon.
Serve the Kartoffelpuffer hot with the mushroom sauce alongside.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the pancakes and sauce separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the pancakes in a hot oven for the best texture. Freeze cooled pancakes between sheets of paper for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Aloo tikki, light
recipes.summary: Golden Indian potato cakes flavoured with ginger, cumin, cilantro and lemon. This lighter batch uses less oil while keeping the outside crisp and the middle soft.

steps.instruction: Simmer the potato in salted water until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Drain the potato and leave it to cool until the surface looks dry and steamy.
Chop the onion, garlic and cilantro and grate the ginger finely.
Mash the potato until smooth with no large lumps remaining.
Mix the potato with the onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro, cumin, paprika, turmeric, lemon juice, bread and salt.
Shape the potato mixture into twelve compact, flat tikki.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Fry the aloo tikki until golden and crisp on both sides, turning them carefully once.
Drain the tikki briefly on absorbent paper before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served freshly fried. Refrigerate cooked tikki for up to 3 days and reheat in a dry pan or hot oven. Freeze shaped uncooked or cooked tikki for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Aloo tikki
recipes.summary: Classic-style Indian potato cakes seasoned with ginger, cumin, turmeric and fresh cilantro. They fry up crisp outside while remaining soft and warmly spiced inside.

steps.instruction: Simmer the potato in salted water until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Drain the potato and leave it to cool until the surface looks dry and steamy.
Chop the onion, garlic and cilantro and grate the ginger finely.
Mash the potato until smooth with no large lumps remaining.
Mix the potato with the onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro, cumin, paprika, turmeric, lemon juice, bread and salt.

recipes.title: Aloo tikki, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous batch of thick Indian potato cakes with extra spice, bread and oil for a deeply crisp crust. They are ideal for sharing as a substantial savoury snack.

recipes.title: Italian zucchini frittata, light
recipes.summary: A light Italian frittata filled with tender zucchini, spinach, basil and a little parmesan. It is soft in the centre, golden at the edges and well suited to breakfast.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C so it is ready to finish the frittata.
Slice the zucchini and onion and tear the basil into small pieces.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof pan and cook the onion and zucchini until softened and lightly golden.
Add the spinach and cook until it has wilted and released moisture has evaporated.
Whisk the eggs with the parmesan cheese, whole milk, basil and salt until evenly combined.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the zucchini, onion and spinach in the pan.
Bake the frittata until the centre is just set and the edges are lightly golden.
Rest the frittata before slicing so the eggs settle and hold their shape.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve warm or at room temperature. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and eat cold or reheat gently. Freeze individual slices for up to 1 month, though the zucchini may soften slightly.

recipes.title: Italian zucchini frittata
recipes.summary: A classic Italian-style frittata with eggs, zucchini, spinach, basil and parmesan. It is simple, savoury and equally good warm or at room temperature.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C so it is fully hot before the frittata goes in.
Slice the zucchini and onion and tear the basil into small pieces.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof pan and cook the onion and zucchini until softened and lightly golden.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted and any released liquid has evaporated.
Whisk the eggs with the parmesan cheese, whole milk, basil and salt until smooth.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the zucchini, onion and spinach.
Bake the frittata until the centre is just set and the top is lightly golden.
Rest the frittata before slicing so the eggs become firm enough to cut neatly.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps for up to 3 days in the refrigerator and can be served cold, at room temperature or gently reheated. Freeze individual slices for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Italian zucchini frittata, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Italian frittata packed with eggs, zucchini, spinach, basil and extra parmesan. It makes a substantial Mediterranean breakfast for sharing.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C so it is fully hot before the larger frittata goes in.
Slice the zucchini and onion and tear the basil into small pieces.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof pan and cook the onion and zucchini until softened and lightly golden.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted and the pan no longer looks watery.
Whisk the eggs with the parmesan cheese, whole milk, basil and salt until evenly combined.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the zucchini, onion and spinach in the pan.
Bake the frittata until the thicker centre is just set and the edges are golden.
Rest the frittata before slicing so the eggs settle and hold together neatly.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and serve cold or gently reheated. Individual slices can be frozen for up to 1 month, although the vegetables will be softer after thawing.
